name: Magnesium Bohr Atom (Mg, Z=12)
semanticDescription: 3D Bohr atomic model of Magnesium (Z=12) showing a central 12p 12n nucleus and 3 concentric electron shells with electronic configuration 2, 8, 2, alongside an ionization detail mode showing 2 valence electrons ejected to yield Mg²⁺ [2, 8].
simplifications: Atomic shells and discrete electron spheres represent the conceptual Bohr-Bury model for educational clarity rather than quantum mechanical probability orbitals.

interactive_states.label: Neutral Mg Atom [2, 8, 2]
interactive_states.description: Magnesium in ground state with 2 valence electrons in outermost M-shell.

interactive_states.label: Valence Excitation
interactive_states.description: Thermal activation loosens the 2 valence electrons.

interactive_states.label: Mg²⁺ Cation [2, 8]
interactive_states.description: Magnesium loses 2 valence electrons, forming a stable neon-like octet core.

cbse_mapping.exam_takeaways: Magnesium readily donates its 2 valence electrons to achieve stable octet configuration.
